messages:
maria: Heads-up, nightly eval flagged pset_v73 with a ~6.1% drop on the 'entity-locate' subset vs v72. Noise looked small but consistent across two runs. Attaching a few failing examples below.
alex: Oof. Can you paste the diff? is this from the phrasing edits in PR #482?
maria: yep looks like that PR. Short diff snippet:
```
- Q: "What city is the conference in?" -> Provide only city name
+ Q: "Where is the conference being held?" -> Provide full address if available
```
maria: That wording change seems to cause extra long-form outputs and hurts the strict extractor metric.
ryan: I see. So model tends to expand when prompt asks for address. Metric counts exact city tokens, so extra detail gets penalized.
jen: Sounds like a prompt semantics shift, not model degradation. Can we revert wording or constrain with an explicit instruction like `Respond with only the city`?
alex: Quick ablation: if we re-run the failing cases with `only_city` suffix, do we recover scores? @eval-bot can you run a small canary (500 examples) with the suffix instruction on the v73 promptpack?
eval-bot: Scheduled canary run: pset_v73 + "Respond with only the city." on model: redwood-open-v1-small. Job id: canary-279012. ETA ~12m.
(maria later): canary finished. result: entity-locate recovered to within 0.6% of v72; other metrics unaffected. Raw examples show fewer multi-token outputs.
ryan: Good. That suggests we can rephrase to constrain rather than revert the whole PR.
alex: Action plan: 1) update prompt template to include explicit `only_city` constraint, 2) open a tiny patch PR to pset_v73 with that change, 3) run full nightly canary on that patch, 4) ask for quick approval from @jen and @maria.
jen: I'll +1 once the PR is up. Also add a unit test in promptbank to assert single-token city extraction for those 12 canonical cases.
maria: PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/promptbank/pulls/496 — title: "pset_v73: constrain entity-locate outputs to city token". Diff attached in PR body.
alex: I'll queue a full nightly canary against that PR. tagging ops-bot for capacity: @ops-bot can we reserve a small canary slot tonight?
ops-bot: Canary slot reserved on gpu-pool-canary at 2026-11-18T02:30Z. Noted.
(maria): If canary passes, we should avoid a full rebaseline — this is a targeted fix. If it still fails, we'll consider reverting PR #482 and open a rebaseline discussion.
ryan: Agree. Also let's capture the failing prompts in eval dashboard with an explainer note so future prompt edits are flagged earlier.
alex: Filing a short postmortem note in the PR and pinging the QA rotation. Thx everyone. :thumbsup:
jen: adding the unit test now, will request review.
maria: closing loop: canary passed (nightly metrics back to baseline). merging PR after jen review. Will update the prompt-change audit and mark pset_v73 as safe to promote.
